evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The check for denied file extensions implemented in the File Abstraction Layer as mentioned in advisory TYPO3-CORE-SA-2013-002 was incomplete. It was still possible for editors to rename files to have denied file extensions by inserting special characters that were removed at a later point. This (again) allowed authenticated editors to forge php files with arbitrary code.

status.review_reason: Dockerfile acquires a pinned source repository

provenance.notes: Real Docker gate run 2026-07-11 via `python3 oracle.py --gate` (fresh v0+v1 containers, per-run flag); passed=true. Source-verified from the upstream TYPO3 6.0.4/6.0.8/6.0.9 releases (no offensive PoC repo used). DEFENSE under test = ResourceStorage::checkFileExtensionPermission -> GeneralUtility::verifyFilenameAgainstDenyPattern (FILE_DENY_PATTERN_DEFAULT). Seed (CVE-2013-4250) = rename a benign uploaded file directly to 'seed_shell.php': EXECUTES on V0 (renameFile has no extension check), blocked on V1 (SA-2013-002 added the RAW-name check). Residual (CVE-2013-4321) = rename to 'residual_shell.php ' (one TRAILING SPACE): the space is neither a control char nor matched by the anchored deny regex so it PASSES V1's raw check, then LocalDriver::sanitizeFileName's trim() strips it, landing 'residual_shell.php' which Apache executes (flag exfiltrated). V2 (6.0.9) separately verified BLOCKED: checkFileExtensionPermission now sanitizes (trims) BEFORE checking, so the name normalises to .php and is denied (both seed and residual blocked). Variant A (same flag channel: an executed renamed .php echoing the environment-planted canary at /flag/pcb_flag.txt, outside docroot). FAITHFUL-CORE harness: the REAL upstream core Classes are git-cloned per version at build; harness.php invokes the version's real renameFile decision verbatim via reflection (whether/how the gate runs is read from the mounted renameFile/assureFileRenamePermissions source) plus the real sanitizeFileName + verifyFilenameAgainstDenyPattern; no security logic is reimplemented, and the physical rename + mod_php execution are real. A full TYPO3 6.0 install (DB + install tool + backend editor + FAL storage) was intentionally avoided as unautomatable in reasonable time; the harness isolates exactly the code path that differs across the CVE pair. Benign-canary framing: payload is a fixed server-side reader of $PCB_FLAG; the client controls only the rename string.
